request: Add rectangular openining to the lower back of the coffee machine, which might serve as draft location for plug and main ON/OFF switch. Opening should be 20cm x 10cm and 3cm deep rectangle with roundend corners (radius 1cm). Position should be more or less equally distanced from bottom and sides of the device.

actions.operation: Create a rounded rectangular opening or recessed cut in the lower back of the coffee machine.

parameters.interpreted_dimensions: 200 mm horizontal width x 100 mm vertical height x 30 mm inward depth, with four 10 mm sketch corner radii
parameters.positioning_method: Center horizontally on the appliance vertical symmetry plane; place in the lowest feasible central rear-cover region, with equal left and right margins and an approximately matching bottom margin where enclosure geometry permits
parameters.cut_direction: Normal to the rear exterior reference field and directed inward toward the appliance
parameters.feature_type: Blind pocket where 30 mm of valid host depth exists; otherwise a rear-cover aperture with a 30 mm recessed electrical-envelope requirement

actions.target: Lower back of the coffee machine.
actions.relational_constraint: Position the opening more or less equally distanced from the bottom and the sides of the device.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the applicable rear face, its lower region, the device bottom boundary, and the relevant side boundaries. The request does not specify which dimension is horizontal, an exact offset, or an exact interpretation of 'more or less equally distanced.' The localization resolves the primary host as the lower central region of the rear service cover. The 200 mm dimension is assumed horizontal and the 100 mm dimension vertical. The rear ventilation grille occupies much of the visible rear field, so any grille ribs intersecting the opening envelope must be trimmed or removed; exact lower-rib Brep IDs cannot be isolated from the supplied representative face mapping. The rear cover may also be thinner than the requested 30 mm depth, so the final implementation must determine whether the feature is a blind pocket, a through-aperture with a recessed electrical back box, or a controlled cut into an approved internal substrate. Do not cut the main U-frame housing without confirming internal clearance and structural acceptability.
steps: Activate the rear service-cover component, Section S03, as the primary editable host. Use face code 0015, Cover outer face, Brep_id FACE 90, to establish the rear-facing sketch orientation. Include face code 0017, Lower cover surface, Brep_id FACE 84, when evaluating the lower boundary and any transition crossed by the cut.

Use the back multiview as the positioning reference. Localize the feature in the lower central rear region, below as much of the ventilation field as practical and between the two vertical perimeter rails. Keep Section S05 rear handle and perimeter trim unchanged and treat its vertical rails and lower transitions as protected clearance geometry.

Create a datum plane parallel to the principal rear exterior field and tangent to, coincident with, or minimally offset from face 0015. A datum plane is preferred over sketching directly on the blended rear surface because the rear cover is described as freeform and shallow-dished.

Project the usable rear-cover outline, the left and right side-return boundaries from face codes 0018 and 0019, the lower cover boundary from face 0017, and the vertical assembly center plane into the sketch as construction geometry.

Draw a center-point rounded rectangle with an overall horizontal width of 200 mm and an overall vertical height of 100 mm. Apply four equal corner fillets of radius 10 mm and constrain the profile to remain symmetric about the appliance vertical center plane.

Constrain the opening center to the rear-cover horizontal midpoint so the left and right clearances are equal. Position the lower edge in the lower rear region and set its bottom clearance approximately equal to the resulting side clearance, adjusting only as required to remain within the valid rear-cover material and outside the perimeter trim.

Check the 200 mm by 100 mm profile against the actual rear-cover boundary. Maintain sufficient material between the rounded rectangle and the side returns, rolled lower transition, attachment interfaces, and trim supports. If equal bottom and side margins are geometrically impossible, preserve horizontal centering and prioritize a safe continuous perimeter around the opening.

Identify all ventilation ribs in Section S04 that cross the rounded-rectangle envelope. Face code 0021, Representative grille rib, Brep_id FACE 118, represents the repeated cylindrical rib geometry. Suppress, shorten, or boolean-trim only the intersecting lower ribs back to the opening boundary; retain all ribs outside the opening and preserve regular end termination.

Extrude the rounded-rectangle cutting tool 30 mm inward, normal to the rear reference plane. Apply the subtractive operation first to the rear service cover only. Confirm that the cut intersects the intended lower portion of face 0015 and, where applicable, the lower transition represented by face 0017.

Inspect the cut depth against the rear-cover thickness and the adjacent Main U-frame housing, Section S02, particularly rear chassis wall face code 0010, Brep_id FACE 58. If the cover is thinner than 30 mm, convert the cover portion to a through-aperture and reserve a 30 mm-deep internal clearance envelope rather than automatically removing structural chassis material.

If a physical 30 mm-deep electrical recess is required and no existing host material supports a blind pocket, create a separate recessed back-box feature behind the aperture. Use the same 200 mm by 100 mm rounded-rectangle perimeter or an appropriately offset wall profile, extend it 30 mm inward, add suitable enclosure wall thickness, and join or fasten it to Section S03 without interfering with Section S02.

Do not remove or modify the rear handle and perimeter trim, the cover side returns, or the lower rolled edge unless an interference check proves the requested opening cannot otherwise fit. The preferred edit modifies Section S03 and trims only the intersecting repeated members of Section S04.

Rebuild the model and verify from the back, left, right, bottom, and isometric views that the opening is centered side-to-side, visibly located in the lower back, clear of the vertical rails, and accessible for a plug and main ON/OFF switch.

Perform a final wall-thickness, edge-distance, interference, and service-access check. Preserve the specified 10 mm profile corner radius. Do not add an unspecified large edge fillet or chamfer; apply only a minimal manufacturing deburr or edge break if required by the downstream process.

intention: Provide a draft location for a plug and the main ON/OFF switch.
